# Soft 404

*Concept* · also written soft 404s

A page that tells users it does not exist (or is empty) but answers with 200; Google treats it as an error and drops it.

**Glossary** (*Soft 404*): A page that returns a success code (200) while its content looks like an error or an empty page. Google keeps it out of the index but may keep crawling it. A CDN captcha page served with 200 is a common cause.

Narrative: the topic [Soft 404s](../topics/soft-404.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

34 claims mention it: 5 from Google's documentation, 25 shown or said at the event (7 not in Google docs, 7 confirmed by Google docs, 10 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 4 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes).

- [`D1-C073`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Docs: A soft 404 is a page that returns a success code while its content looks like an error or an empty page. It is kept out of the index but continues to be crawled, wasting crawl budget. `[D1-C073, docs, Google, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes]`
- [`D1-C369`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Docs: Google's status code page says that with a 204 No Content response Google receives no content and cannot process it, and that a 2xx page whose content is empty or an error message shows as a soft 404 in Search Console. `[D1-C369, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes]`
- [`D2-C192`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Docs: Google's JavaScript guides say that when client-side routing makes a real 404 status impractical, a single-page app can avoid soft 404s by redirecting with JavaScript to a URL whose server returns 404, or by adding a robots noindex meta tag with JavaScript. `[D2-C192, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C294`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Docs: For client-side rendered single-page apps, where meaningful status codes can be impossible or impractical, Google's documentation gives two ways to avoid soft 404s: a JavaScript redirect to a URL that returns a 404 status, or a noindex robots meta tag added with JavaScript. `[D2-C294, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C911`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Docs: Google's site move guide says not to redirect many old URLs to one irrelevant destination such as the new site's home page, which can confuse users and might be treated as a soft 404, and to return a 404 or 410 for deleted or merged content that is not moved to the new site. `[D2-C911, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C335`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Because error pages are worded in endless variations, of which 'page not found' is only the classic one, Google cannot detect soft 404s with simple error, word or keyword matching. `[D2-C335, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C337`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Slide, Day 2, not in Google docs: Mistakes in Google's own systems are a further cause of soft 404s, and Gary Illyes asked site owners to report such mistakes in Google's forums. `[D2-C337, slide, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C338`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google detects soft 404s with a language model, described as something like BERT, that is trained to understand the structure and layout of a page as well as its language, instead of reading the page as one flat wall of text. `[D2-C338, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C339`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: For soft 404 detection, the position of error text decides: an error in a less important part such as the navigation need not make a page a soft 404, but an error message alone in the main content, like 'Error establishing a database connection', does, much as a human would judge it. `[D2-C339, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C340`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google's soft 404 detection tells the page chrome, such as navigation and footer, apart from the main content by analysing the page's visual hierarchy alongside its text. `[D2-C340, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C364`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google clusters duplicate pages by content in four ways: exact matches, near matches, structurally similar content, and soft 404s. `[D2-C364, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C714`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: 'Crawled – currently not indexed' is most of the time a quality issue rather than a technical one: the pages are usually low quality or useless for the index, for example duplicates or soft 404s. `[D2-C714, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C355`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: A soft 404 is a 404 in disguise: the page returns 200 but its content says something like 'page not found', information the site should have sent as the HTTP status. `[D1-C355, stage, Cherry Prommawin, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C508`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Google said soft 404s, like some other problem categories, are looked up in Search Console's page indexing report, while other crawl issues are debugged in the Crawl Stats report. `[D1-C508, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C213`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: A page that renders empty for Google, such as a client-side product page hit by these mistakes, is seen as thin content and ends up treated as a soft 404 even though users see a full page. `[D2-C213, stage, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C264`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google's slide defined a soft 404 in a JavaScript application as a page that serves a 'Not Found' message but returns a 200 HTTP status code. `[D2-C264, slide, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C291`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: In JavaScript single-page apps, soft 404s typically arise because the server returns the app with a 200 status for every URL, so when the app shows a 'not found' message for a URL that does not exist, no error is reported. `[D2-C291, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C334`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: A soft 404 is a page that should return an error status code but returns HTTP 200; from a crawling point of view it looks indexable, but because it has no real content Google throws it out of the index. `[D2-C334, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C336`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google listed four common causes of soft 404s: pages that look like errors but are not, thin or empty content, server or CMS misconfigurations, and JavaScript-dependent content that fails to load. `[D2-C336, slide, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C070`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Soft 404s were named as a crawl problem alongside DNS and firewall issues, and described as one of the biggest problems on the internet right now for crawling and showing up in Search. `[D1-C070, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C356`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Soft 404 pages are still crawled like normal pages; their bigger consequences are for indexing, and they also affect crawling. `[D1-C356, stage, Cherry Prommawin, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C367`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: CDN captcha challenges often return HTTP 200; Googlebot does not solve them and sees only content with a 200 status, which indexing then classifies as a soft 404, reported as an error in Search Console. `[D1-C367, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C191`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The fix for a client-side soft 404 is to make a missing page end with a real HTTP 404 status code instead of 200. `[D2-C191, stage, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C260`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google listed four common JavaScript problems for indexing: content not present in the rendered HTML, using # in URLs for content changes, soft 404s and blocked resources. `[D2-C260, slide, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C292`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The fix for a client-side soft 404 is to serve a real 404 error page where appropriate; how to detect URLs that do not exist depends on how the app works and where it is hosted. `[D2-C292, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C341`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Gary Illyes said soft 404 detection keeps searchers from clicking into dead ends and avoids wasting site owners' resources on visitors sent to error pages. `[D2-C341, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C367`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Soft 404 pages are another reason Google clusters pages together, an outcome site owners usually do not want. `[D2-C367, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C696`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection applies the negative signals that immediately block indexing: noindex (the likely reading of one unclear word), expired unavailable_after dates, soft 404s, non-canonical duplicates, spam signals and other policies. `[D2-C696, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C700`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection drops soft 404 pages that were not dropped earlier, for example when a document is reprocessed. `[D2-C700, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C607`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: An audience member reported recrawl intervals on one very large, popular client site: the homepage about 5 times a day, first-level pages about every 1.5 days (uncertain reading), and pages clustered as soft 404s every 160 to 190 days, adding that other sites will differ. `[D3-C607, stage, an audience member, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C078`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Analysis: For temporary blocks return 503 or 429, never a 200 page with a captcha or error message, which becomes a soft 404 and can replace real content in the index. Verify Googlebot by reverse DNS, not by user agent. `[D1-C078, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D1-C371`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Analysis: Day 1 said a CDN captcha page served with HTTP 200 becomes a soft 404, while Day 2 (D2-C374, D2-C375) said such challenge pages are hard to recognise as errors and can be clustered as duplicates; Google's CDN post describes both outcomes, and in both the real pages drop out of Search. `[D1-C371, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C295`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Analysis: After moving to real paths, set the server or hosting rewrite rules so a direct request to every valid path returns 200 with the content (ideally server-rendered) and an unknown path returns a 404 status, which removes client-side soft 404s at the source. `[D2-C295, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C342`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Analysis: Return real error status codes for error states, 404 or 410 for missing content and 503 for outages such as a failed database connection, also in single-page apps; a 200 page whose main content is only an error message is treated as a soft 404 even when header and navigation look normal. `[D2-C342, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-CAN-10` **MUST** · Documented: Redirect an old URL only to a page with the same intent, and return 404 or 410 when there is none (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-ERR-01` **MUST** · Documented: Return 404 or 410 for removed and non-existent URLs (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-ERR-02` **MUST** · Documented: Return a real 404 for unknown routes in single-page apps, or use a documented client-side fallback (6 of its claims mention it)
- `DEV-ERR-03` **AVOID** · Documented: Never serve error states, empty results or failed data loads with a 200 status (7 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-03` **SHOULD** · Documented: Watch the Page indexing report and treat its not-indexed reasons as a work list (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-REN-04` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not block JavaScript, CSS or API endpoints that pages need for rendering in robots.txt (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-02` **AVOID** · Documented: Never serve bot challenges or error pages to crawlers with a 200 status (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-03` **MUST** · Documented: Answer planned maintenance and short outages with 503, for a day or two at most (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
